subject: Re: Acme Corp — long-context evals & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Acme call recap — long‑context evals and next steps

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery on long‑context requirements and proposed next steps: 

- Context size: you confirmed average document bundles ~45k tokens (raw), with frequent ~75k token legal exhibits on larger deals.
- Primary goals: (1) accurate summarization without hallucinations, (2) reliable truncation behavior and clear failover when context overflows, (3) extractive QA and reranking across entire bundle.
- Current infra: internal preprocessing slices files by chapter; you want to avoid manual sharding if possible.

Recommended immediate experiments: 
1) Long‑context eval with our 100k context kernel (preferred) + two lower‑fp16 quantized variants to measure quality/cost tradeoffs.
2) Prompt set: we’ll run comparative summaries (concise executive brief, timeline + redlines, extractive Q&A) across the same input. Expect to see differences in fidelity at ~50‑75k tokens.
3) Benchmarks: we’ll provide token‑level latency/cost, truncation behavior logs, and a quality regression dashboard keyed to your prompt set.

Action items / owners: 
- Marissa (me): coordinate evals, share baseline prompt sets and model recommendations by Friday.
- Dylan (engineering): provide an evaluation harness and attaches KV/truncation logs for the test runs.
- Samir / Elena: share 3 representative bundles (redacted) and the top 10 QA prompts you care about.

We’ll attach the initial prompt pack and a short recommended models doc so you can review before we run full benchmarks. Let me know if I missed anything.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood-model-recommendations.pdf

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Acme call recap — long‑context evals and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great. A couple follow‑ups from our side: 

1) Can you send the benchmark template and a sample of the prompt sets you’ll run? We want to validate the prompts match our legal review style.
2) For the models: curious about the specific variants you recommend for 100k vs 50k contexts and rough delta in token cost.
3) On truncation: if the model hits the window, what’s the expected behavior — graceful summary of truncated portion, or error/flag? We’d prefer a deterministic flag so downstream tooling can fall back to chunked processing.

We’ll prepare 3 redacted bundles and the 10 QA prompts, target to share by Wednesday.

—Samir
Director of Legal Tech, Acme Corp
samir.patel@acme.com

On Mon, 16 Nov 2026 at 08:10, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again — looking forward to the bundles.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Acme call recap — long‑context evals and next steps

Dylan / Dev — forwarding Samir’s reply and initial asks. High level: they want deterministic flagging when context exceeds window, plus a comparison between:

A) our 100k context kernel (lossy kv compaction + windowed attention) — goal: minimal sharding
B) 50k context quantized variant (faster, cheaper)

Please prepare:
- Evaluation harness that logs: input token counts, truncation events, kv cache eviction points, and per‑prompt ROUGE/QA F1 metrics. Output should be CSV + JSONL (for traceability).
- A small benchmark run using redacted bundle A (30k tokens), B (60k tokens), C (78k tokens).
- A defined deterministic truncation flag in the runtime that returns a header X‑Redwood‑Context‑Status: OK | TRUNCATED | PARTIAL with an explanation field. If PARTIAL, include the token range omitted.

Attachments to include in the run: prompt-sets-acme.zip (contains the executive brief + extractive QA templates) and acme-long-context-eval-benchmark.csv (schema template).

Let me know if this is feasible to turn around by Friday. If not, propose a realistic ETA.

Thanks — Marissa

> On Mon, 16 Nov 2026 at 09:05, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com> wrote:
> > Thanks Marissa — this is great. A couple follow‑ups from our side:...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:23:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Acme Corp — long‑context evals & next steps

Hi Samir / Elena —

Per our timeline, attaching the prompt bundle and the model recommendation PDF. Quick answers inline to your questions: 

- Benchmark template & prompts: attached (prompt-sets-acme.zip). The prompts include the executive brief template, extractive QA set, redline detection queries, and a summarization fidelity checklist.
- Model variants: we recommend the following run order: 1) Redwood-LR-100k (highest fidelity, best KV behavior), 2) Redwood-LQ-100k-quant (reduced FP16 with aggressive KV compaction), 3) Redwood-LQ-50k-quant (cost‑optimized). See redwood-model-recommendations.pdf for estimated token cost deltas and latency profiles.
- Truncation behavior: the runtime will return X‑Redwood‑Context‑Status headers as proposed. If TRUNCATED or PARTIAL, the response body includes a concise note: \"Context truncated — omitted tokens N..M. Recommend chunked fallback.\" We’ll also log the truncation event to the benchmark CSV.

Next steps: 
- Please share the 3 redacted bundles and your 10 QA prompts (Samir) — target Wed 11/25.
- We’ll run the baseline benchmarks and return a dashboard and CSV by Mon 11/29.

If that timing works I’ll schedule a 30‑minute touchpoint the week of 11/30 to review results.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: prompt-sets-acme.zip; acme-long-context-eval-benchmark.csv; redwood-model-recommendations.pdf
